newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds get second wind in late trade.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds get second wind in late trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities drifted into positive territory and yield spreads were mostly unchanged to Treasuries in late trade Friday.
A few market participants made defensive-style bids, buoying overall pass-through prices.
"When the (Treasury) market started rallying, we started picking up a little more convexity," one trader in New York said, referring to the change in the shape of the yield curve.
Bids were made for Ginnie 8.5 percent coupons because of an expected increase in prepayment speed and price stability, he said.
"We also like buying Fannie 8.0s TBA (To Be Announced) because the roll is so good," the trader added.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 2/32 at 99-18/32, yielding 93 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were up 1/32 at 99-17/32, and Freddie Mac paper was 2/32 at 99-22/32.
Five-year Treasuries were up 1/32 at 6.53 percent, and 10-year notes were up 3/32 at 6.66 percent.
Friday's employment report caused the greatest stir in early trade, giving a slight boost to Treasuries and mortgages.
The Labor Department reported U.S. non-farm payroll growth slowed in April to 142,000, but the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 perecent, its lowest level in over 23 years.
But some proit-taking erased earlier gains.

Art Frank, vice president of mortgage research at HSBC Securities Inc, said the expected returns for holding pass-throughs are higher than the spreads would indicate because the dollar roll market continues "to be on special" in current coupons and in slight premiums.
"Clearly people are getting into TBA pass-throughs for the roll opportunities," he added.
